lane: P-101 ladder re-cut build (gates and copy)
whatChangedSinceCP1: D4 (importOriginal in the two route-test mocks) SURVIVED its falsifier. The isolate loads the real peEntitlement through the six-name @workspace/db mock without error, so the predicate under test is the single api-server definition and no fourth copy was written into a test factory.

D6 (deriving PricingModal GROUPS from config) was proven load-bearing by violation 4, not merely reasoned about: reverting to the hand-written three-entry array fails three cases while pricing.ts still declares four groups. That is the exact defect the 2026-08-31 amendment predicted and it now has a control.

Item 11 lost its rendered-output assertion. WhatYouCanDo holds `open` in local state with no prop, so renderToStaticMarkup can only ever produce the collapsed card. Recorded in the test file as a stated limitation rather than solved by adding an `initialOpen` prop that exists only for a test. Item 11's own check does not ask for a render; item 6 does, and item 6 has one.

adversarialReviewOfOwnWork.challenge: Is the MCP test vacuous? It cannot fail because the gate is missing.
adversarialReviewOfOwnWork.answer: Correct, and it says so in its own header. It pins a DIFFERENT property — no parallel gate, refusal reaches the connector — and that property is falsifiable: violation 8 added a local canRunStudioReport check to create_screen and the test failed. The gate's own falsification is violations 1 and 9 in the api-server.
adversarialReviewOfOwnWork.residualRisk: A reader skimming file names could mistake screens-studio-gate.test.ts for the gate's proof. Mitigated by the file header, not by renaming, because the file genuinely is about the screens gate's connector half.

adversarialReviewOfOwnWork.challenge: The four-groups render test walks Object.keys(PE_PRICING.groups). Two derivations, or one?
adversarialReviewOfOwnWork.answer: One. It is a completeness check against a single source, not a divergence test, and CP1 said so before it was written. What makes it worth having is that it fails on DRIFT between config and render, which is the defect class; it would not have failed before this card, when both held three.
adversarialReviewOfOwnWork.residualRisk: None claimed. The test additionally asserts the literal key list ['answer','list','handoff','firm'] so an emptied config cannot make the loop pass by iterating nothing.

adversarialReviewOfOwnWork.challenge: Does the 402 body leak anything, or default anything?
adversarialReviewOfOwnWork.answer: It carries tier and subscriptionTier as resolvePeEntitlement computed them from pe_user_entitlements. Nothing is defaulted: a paid row with no stored rung reads as solo inside resolvePeEntitlement, never silently as studio, and an unauthenticated caller gets 401 before any rung is named.

adversarialReviewOfOwnWork.challenge: The panel branch keys on the string 'studio_screens'. What happens if the api-server changes it?
adversarialReviewOfOwnWork.answer: The panel silently falls back to the generic 'Not returned' head. That is a real coupling across two packages with no shared module. It is DECLARED here rather than hidden: the string is a named export on both sides (STUDIO_SCREENS_REFUSAL_REASON in peStudioGate.ts, UPGRADE_SCREENS_REASON in mcp-app.ts) and both are commented as each other's counterpart. A cross-package divergence test would need a second derivation neither package has today. Logged as OPEN, not closed.

adversarialReviewOfOwnWork.challenge: Did the api-server change break anything outside the screens routes?
adversarialReviewOfOwnWork.answer: No. Full suite run before and after with the same DATABASE_URL stub: 127 files failed in both, 43 tests failed in both, passing tests 2039 to 2047. The delta is exactly the eight new cases. peStudioGate performs no work at module load, so an incomplete peEntitlement mock in an unrelated test cannot break on import.

One. The property-explorer suite failed once on scripts/seam-retired-guard.test.mjs (check 2, vercel.json rewrite) immediately after the edits. It passed alone and passed twice more in full. It mutates vercel.json on disk, so it races. Recorded as a pre-existing flake OBSERVED here, not as a clean run, and not attributed to this lane without that evidence.

conflictResolved.whyNotDone: Unsatisfiable alongside item 2. A route-gated tool must call cortex to learn it is refused; not.toHaveBeenCalled() passes only if a local MCP gate exists, which item 2 forbids and which violation 8 demonstrates.
conflictResolved.whatWasDoneInstead: The inverse, made load-bearing: toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1) on the free path, plus assertions that the upstream 402 and its reason survive into the tool result. Violation 8 proves it fires.
conflictResolved.operatorDecisionNeeded: no. Item 2 is the ruled architecture; item 4's shape was copied from two locally-gated tools.
